rows.note: 0.006 in out of roughly 8.5 in diameter is about 0.07 percent (my arithmetic; sphere diameter not read directly in the pages I opened). Thickness variation of about +/-5 percent from nominal could be obtained (Carlson, plating section). This precision gave 86 percent of classical; the authors link low results to surface flaws and nonuniformities.

rows.note: Eq. (2.2-10) Bartelds and Mayers gives 0.86; Eq. (2.2-8) at K_delta = 0 gives critical stresses 'approximately 5 percent less'. CR-1999 (Section 2.2) credits the 0.82 to Yusuff 1955 (thick sandwich with cellular cores).

source.title: Manual for Structural Stability Analysis of Sandwich Plates and Shells (NASA CR-1457)
source.org_or_authors: R. T. Sullins, G. W. Smith, E. E. Spier, General Dynamics Convair for NASA MSC
source.quote: has been selected here to provide safe design values. This implies that a knock-down factor of approximately 0.4 is applicable to this wrinkling phenomenon.

rows.note: Use when waviness is unknown: 'Whenever the initial waviness is unknown, it is recommended that the following equation be used to obtain a lower-bound prediction'. The authors: 'Obviously, this is not a rigorous approach ... can only be regarded as a best-available approach'. The report does NOT state the waviness amplitude that 0.33 assumes. Gap. Setting 0.33 = 0.82/(1 + 0.64 K_delta) gives K_delta of about 2.3 (my arithmetic); the physical amplitude then depends on Ec, tc, Fc, none of which is given for the 0.33 data set.

source.org_or_authors: R. P. Ley, W. Lin, U. Mbanefo, Northrop Grumman
source.quote: Jenkinson and Kuenzi attributed these discrepancies to initial waviness of the facesheets.

rows.note: Value 0.125 is the Jenkinson-Kuenzi k2, the lowest in the table. CR-1999 judges these tests 'probably violated' theory assumptions, so they are not clean waviness measurements. Waviness-amplitude parameter: 'the best results have been obtained when the parameter is determined empirically from a large number of destructive tests' (Conclusions). Rogers 1964 (GD ERR-FW-196, 'Face Wrinkling as a Function of Surface Waviness') is cited but I did not open it.

source.title: A study on buckling strength of single layer reticulated domes based on the concept of member buckling strength (Japanese text)
source.org_or_authors: S. Kato, Y. Niho; Steel Construction Engineering (JSSC) 8(29):59-72
source.location: Introduction p. 60-61; Fig. 2 region p. 62 (Japanese text)
source.quote: knock down factor which can be used in estimating elasto-plastic buckling loads (English abstract)

rows.note: I read the Japanese full text only partly. alpha_0 is a knock-down on the member buckling axial force used in sizing, tied to dome geometry (xi built from half open angle and member slenderness), not strictly the shell classical-to-test ratio. The analysis assumed NO initial shape imperfection ('imperfection deferred to future work'). The 0.65 is a design-style number; the seat's 'optimistic 0.4 from Wright 1965' is NOT confirmed here.

source.title: Buckling of spherical shells revisited
source.org_or_authors: J. W. Hutchinson; Proc. R. Soc. A 472:20160577
source.quote: for an extended range of imperfection widths, the plateau lies between 15% and 20% of the classical pressure

limits.note: Bounds the pessimistic end: an imperfection of about 1 t depth already sets this plateau. 'More numerical and experimental work will be required to establish the robustness of the plateau for other imperfection shapes.'

limits.what: No source opened states the least imperfection that is achievable for a thin shell. Best printed figures: sphere diameter variation 0.006 in with +/-5 percent thickness (1966); 16-17 um RMS on a 12 m reflector (2006); +/-0.1 in on an 8 ft cylinder (2018)

source.title: An Experimental Study of the Buckling of Complete Spherical Shells (NASA Contractor Report, Aug 1966; journal version Exp. Mech. 7(7):281-288, 1967)
source.org_or_authors: R. L. Carlson, R. L. Sendelbeck, N. J. Hoff, Stanford University for NASA (grant NsG-630)
source.quote: For the best shell produced the maximum difference in the measured diameter was 0.006 inch.

limits.note: Gap: no statement of a physical floor on imperfection, and no amplitude-in-wall-thickness figure for any real large shell.

gaps: sphere_knockdown_best_test: no experimental complete-sphere or hemisphere knockdown for the ~2006 era found; no new test series above 0.86 found for any era.

sphere_knockdown_best_test: Krenzke and Kiernan 1963 and Seaman 1962 were not opened (DTIC 403; Seaman is an MIT thesis). Krenzke 0.73 and 0.90 appear only in a web-search summary of the DTIC abstract; value left null. Lee 2016 gives machined-aluminium range 0.45-0.9.

sphere_knockdown_best_test: Wagner, Huhne and coworkers (2018 IJMS 141, 2020 IJPVP 179:104015, 2021 IJPVP 104321) were read only as abstracts; no numeric KDF or test ratio. The Mendeley database of over 800 sphere tests (10.17632/fshsssd6s9.1) was not opened. Wunderlich and Albertin 2002 not opened.

sphere_knockdown_best_test: Carlson et al. were nickel (electroformed), not copper as the card says; electroformed copper shells were Thompson 1960-61 (cited in Hutchinson and Thompson 2017, not opened as primary).

sphere_knockdown_best_test: SP-8032 has no NTRS copy found; read from an everyspec scan. Its 0.14 is a lower bound on caps/deep shells; no separate complete-sphere design number found in the pages read.

sandwich_dome_knockdown: no sandwich dome or sandwich sphere buckling test newer than the S-II common bulkhead tests (Gonzalez and Patton 1964, SDL 468, via CR-1457) was found; the 2010s-2020s sandwich tests are CYLINDERS (CTA8.1, CTA8.2B). Gonzalez and Patton and Yao 1962 not opened. Figure 6.2-3 hemisphere points (about 0.22-0.26) read by eye.
sandwich_dome_knockdown: CTA8.2 (NTRS 20210024095) returned JSON, not read; CTA8.3 and CTA8.4 not read. SBKF sandwich-cylinder series summary KDFs not found.

cylinder_knockdown_design: SBKF final analysis-based KDFs for metallic and composite cylinders are in the SP-8007 Rev 2 section 4.3 but I only read the draft's Gamma_2 = 0.78. Hilburger 2012 AIAA 2012-1686 and 2018 SciTech paper (only a 2-page abstract) not read for numbers.

shape_precision: no RMS figure found for machined, spun or electroformed closed shells 10-20 m class or for the eras 1970s-2000s; reflector panel-only RMS not read; no source gives amplitude per wall thickness for large spun domes. Wagner et al. measured-imperfection datasets for domes not read.

wrinkle_coefficient_test: CR-1457 does not state the waviness amplitude or K_delta that 0.33 assumes. Rogers 1964 (face wrinkling vs surface waviness) cited in CR-1999 but not opened. No newer (2000s-2020s) honeycomb-sandwich wrinkling test with measured face flatness found. CR-1457 dates FPL 1810 as March 1956 while CR-1999 dates it 1949.

lattice_dome_knockdown: Wright 1965 (the claimed source of 0.4) not readable (ASCE 403, steel.org.au member-only); the 0.4 is NOT confirmed. JGJ 7-2010 text (knockdown or safety factor about 0.2) not found; Bulenda and Knippers 2001 (Comput. Struct. 79:1161-1174) abstract only; Kato and Niho 2001 read only partly in Japanese; Gioncu 1995 review (403). No lattice-dome test ratios found.

member_straightness: no printed straightness for silicon carbide tubes found (supplier datasheets and a patent search gave none; a patent hit was for few-cm zirconia fibre-optic ferrules, not used). EN 1090-2 tolerance not found. No historical (1960s-1990s) series for steel or ceramic straightness found; CFRP only from a retail datasheet.

Not sourced for any property: per-era trend tables. The only property with a measured ratio in two eras for the same kind of structure is the cylinder (1928-64 test lower bound versus 70-90 percent for modern cylinders in 2020, and 72-87 percent for sandwich cylinders).
